limitations: All v2/v3 SKU counts remain zero. Formal bounds and reviewed published native bindings are prerequisites, never derived from browser quantity or model names.
Nano Token persists receipts and ready images; missing/invalid/over-bound usage holds reservations. Tests inject stored images and never submit to a provider.

Native Token scope is existing image/video model resources and supported generation APIs. Grok and Nano application fixtures prove specific bindings and ledgers only, not every real application or derived pricing variant.

Native Pixel reads declared successful result slots and measures safe image bytes, preserving duplicate slots. Response dimension fields and measurement-like fields are ignored. Tests use actual in-memory synthetic PNG data URIs; no external image fetch or upload occurs.

Measurement runs before the transaction opened by OpenMarketBilling::settle; execution lease and native/result fingerprints are checked again under ledger locks. An outer caller transaction is not ruled out. The lost-lease test proves rejection before attempted image download.

Pixel missing/malformed receipt retains pending usage; invalid or excessive bytes/slots keep funds through the existing settlement_failed recovery wrapper. Corrected in-memory results settle using frozen prices.
Compilation emits in-memory drafts only, with explicit Token or Pixel binding. Synthetic application route/method/lifecycle/receipt declarations were completed rather than relaxing production checks.

The legacy no-binding pixel refusal test was updated to require a precise published binding, then verify request-bound reservation without transport. Legacy fixed/per-call/count paths and old tasks remain preserved.
No HTTP login, actual supplier lifecycle, file storage transfer, real worker restart, published contract or unified frontend acceptance was performed.
